name: Bahraini Citizenship by Marriage (foreign wife of a Bahraini man)

requirement_groups.name: Standard route -- foreign wife of a Bahraini man

requirements.blocker_text: Married to a Bahraini man. NOTE: Bahraini law provides NO route to citizenship for a foreign man married to a Bahraini woman at all -- see the structural note below.

Must actively declare her wish to acquire citizenship to the Minister of Interior and maintain the marriage for 5 years from that declaration. The Minister may shorten the period or refuse on national-security grounds -- this is not automatic even once the 5 years pass.
requirements.fix_path: Declare the wish and maintain the marriage for 5 years from that declaration.

evidence_required.document: Declaration of wish filed with the Minister of Interior

sources.title: GLOBALCIT (EUI academic citizenship-law observatory) -- English translation of the Bahraini Citizenship Act 1963, as amended (1981): foreign wife of a Bahraini man may acquire citizenship by declaring her wish to the Minister of Interior and maintaining the marriage 5 years from that declaration, subject to Ministerial discretion to shorten or refuse; no equivalent provision exists for a foreign husband of a Bahraini woman

Nationality, Passports and Residence Affairs (NPRA), Bahrain -- 'Citizenship for a Bahraini's Wife' service page: confirms the service exists and requires in-person/online application, but does not itemize the substantive eligibility criteria beyond that

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Bahrain). STATUS: DRAFT -- the substantive eligibility detail (5-year declared-wish requirement, Ministerial discretion) is tier-2 GLOBALCIT sourced; a tier-1 NPRA page confirms the service exists ('Citizenship for a Bahraini's Wife' -- note the name itself already signals the gendered scope) but doesn't itemize the criteria, so the hard requirements cite the tier-2 source and the file stays draft. GENDERED STRUCTURAL ASYMMETRY, MORE EXTREME THAN OTHER GULF STATES IN THIS DATASET: Bahrain has NO marriage-based citizenship provision AT ALL for a foreign man married to a Bahraini woman -- not a harder path, not a fallback via a permanent-residency exemption (contrast with Qatar's 2018 PR-law exemption category for non-Qatari husbands of Qatari women) -- simply no route. This is a more severe asymmetry than Qatar's equivalent gap found elsewhere in this dataset. Even for the wife's route, acquisition is NOT automatic at 5 years -- it requires an affirmative declaration and remains subject to Ministerial discretion to refuse on national-security grounds, closer in character to Bahrain's broader Royal-discretion citizenship culture (see bh_citizenship_special_grounds.json) than to a rights-based administrative process.
